title: Correct ci.yml's stale claim that dev requires three status checks
description:
The long comment on ci.yml's push trigger says: 'dev's branch ruleset requires 3 status checks (docker e2e harness, lint/typecheck/test windows-latest, operating block digest) on every push'.

Read live on 2026-09-11, dev's ruleset requires exactly TWO contexts:
- 'docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries)'
- 'lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest)'   <- note U+00B7, not an ASCII period

The 'operating block digest' context is gone, presumably removed when the fleet-operating content moved out of this public repo in #654. main has NO rules configured at all.

This matters more than a stale comment usually would, because the comment's whole purpose is to explain WHY ci.yml deliberately does not run on pushes to dev — it argues that a direct push to dev can never satisfy the required checks, which is what makes landing on dev structurally impossible except through a PR. The argument still holds with two contexts, but a reader checking the reasoning against reality finds a context that does not exist and cannot tell whether the rest of the paragraph is also stale. The comment also explicitly warns siblings not to copy the shape without checking their own ruleset — advice that is undermined by the example itself being out of date.

Found while adding the OPAG-79 Tracker integrity job (LCLI-471). Kept out of that PR deliberately: work discovered outside a task's acceptance criteria is a new task, not a silent addition.

If 'Tracker integrity' is added to dev's ruleset as a required context, that count changes again — so do this AFTER that decision lands, and write the number that is then true rather than today's two.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The ci.yml push-trigger comment names the contexts dev actually requires, verified against the live ruleset at the time of the edit, not against this description
The U+00B7 in the lint context is preserved exactly where the comment quotes it, since required contexts match by rendered name
main having no rules configured is stated, so an absent gate is not mistaken for an unchecked one
Any change to the required set from adding Tracker integrity is reflected in the same edit

finalSummary:
Landed as PR #3, squash-merged to dev as 2d27025 on 2026-09-11.

All 4 acceptance criteria met. The comment now names the three contexts dev actually requires, read live at edit time rather than copied from this description: 'docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries)', 'lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest)', and 'Tracker integrity'. The U+00B7 is preserved where quoted and called out explicitly, since contexts match by rendered job name and the character is invisible in review. main having NO ruleset is now stated, so an absent gate is not read as a passing one. The count changed from two to three while this task was open — 'Tracker integrity' was added to require-ci-on-dev with the user's approval after LCLI-471 proved green — and the edit reflects the count that is true now, not the two that were true when the task was written.

The comment also now dates itself (2026-09-11) and points at [{"type":"required_status_checks","parameters":{"strict_required_status_checks_policy":false,"do_not_enforce_on_create":false,"required_status_checks":[{"context":"docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries)"},{"context":"lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest)"},{"context":"Tracker integrity"}]},"ruleset_source_type":"Repository","ruleset_source":"opum-ai/lore-cli","ruleset_id":22838594}], so the next reader re-derives the list instead of trusting a comment. That is the actual fix: the defect was not the wrong number, it was a comment asserting a checkable fact with nothing telling the reader how to check it.

Incidental verification worth recording: PR #3 reported mergeStateStatus BLOCKED while required contexts were pending and CLEAN once they passed, and Tracker integrity passed as a required context on its first run under the new ruleset. So the gate demonstrably gates — it was not merely configured.
